title: Fact Check

claims.claim: This bill spends more than any infrastructure bill in history.
claims.explanation: Adjusted for inflation, the 1956 Federal-Aid Highway Act and the 2009 American Recovery Act both exceed this bill's spending on infrastructure in real terms.

sources.title: Congressional Budget Office — Historical spending on surface transportation
Bureau of Labor Statistics — CPI-U adjustment series

claims.claim: The bill includes funding for rural broadband.
claims.explanation: The bill text allocates $42.5 billion to rural broadband deployment, matching the speaker's description.

claims.claim: The speaker voted against this bill.
claims.explanation: No roll-call vote has been recorded for this version of the bill. The speaker has voted against earlier drafts.

basis: Two of three claims could be checked against primary sources.
One claim depends on a vote that has not occurred.
limitations: Fact-checking relies on public sources at the time of analysis; later data may change verdicts.
The clip's captions and audio were not independently verified against the source recording.

summary: Two claims are checkable. One is contradicted by historical spending data; one is supported by bill text. A third claim depends on an upcoming vote and remains unclear.
